nodes.label: Research and monitoring teams

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Protected areas management|Research and monitoring teams_qna_000
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What alternative approach is proposed to monitor research efforts?
nodes.answer: The proposed alternative approach monitors the intended ex-ante research efforts in funded research projects to provide a complementary view of research activity.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Protected areas management|Research and monitoring teams_qna_001
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: Who is handling the study mentioned in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The study is handled by Michelle Tigchelaar from Stanford University, United States of America.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Protected areas management|Research and monitoring teams_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Who are the members of the research team involved in this study?
nodes.answer: The research team includes senior researchers and graduate students representing various fields such as environmental studies, biology, history/Indigenous studies, fine arts, and nursing.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Protected areas management|Research and monitoring teams_qna_003
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What permits were issued for the research conducted in the Galapagos?
nodes.answer: The research was authorized under permits PC-51-18 and PC-59-19 issued by the Galapagos National Park Directorate.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Protected areas management|Research and monitoring teams_qna_004
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: Who supervised the pilot study documenting the new monitoring strategy?
nodes.answer: The study was supervised by scientific staff with expertise in mammalogy and molecular biology.
